corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies, the corpus reveals rapid growth of LLM-enabled methods, critical reflection on AI’s social effects, and applications spanning education, health, policy, and culture. Researchers explore methodological opportunities and governance needs for LLMs, examine trust, bias, and equity in deployment, and assess AI’s influence on learning, decision-making, and public discourse. A common emphasis is on validation, transparency, and human-centered oversight to mitigate risks.

themes.name: LLM-enabled social science methods and governance
themes.description: Studies examine how LLMs augment research methods, simulations, and public-participation tools while highlighting validation, transparency, and governance needs.

themes.name: Trust, ethics, equity, and societal impact of AI
themes.description: Research across domains investigates trust, anthropomorphism, cultural adequacy, misinformation, and equitable governance, underscoring ethical considerations and governance frameworks.

themes.name: AI in education, learning, and literacy
themes.description: Research investigates AI’s effects on learning outcomes, pedagogy, classroom dynamics, AI literacy, and risks such as overreliance and assessment challenges.

themes.name: Health, wellbeing, misinformation, and AI in health communication
themes.description: A cluster analyzes AI’s role in health information, patient education, sharing behaviors, and health misinformation, with safety and readability considerations.
